newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan navy stops Tamils fleeing to India.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan navy stops Tamils fleeing to India.

text.p: A Sri Lankan navy vessel has intercepted a boat carrying 105 Tamil refugees fleeing to southern India, military officials said on Monday.
The refugees, including 33 women and 40 children, had come from Kilinochchi, the scene of a fierce battle between government troops and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), they said.

The LTTE rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka, had prevented the Tamils from going to government-run refugee camps in Vavuniya, about 215 km (135 miles) northeast of Colombo, the officials said.
An estimated 200,000 Tamil refugees are on the move in the rebel-held jungle area of the Wanni after the army captured Jaffna peninsula in April and Kilinochchi last month.
"The Tamils wanted to go to India yesterday after they were stopped by the LTTE from going to Vavuniya to escape misery," a military officer said.
In a statement faxed to the international media in Colombo, the LTTE said malaria and diarrhoea "have reached epidemic proportions" among Tamils in Wanni who had fled bombing in Kilinochchi.
The rebels complained of a lack of medicine due to the authorities' suspension of medical supplies to the rebel-held territory.
A military spokesman said enough medicine had been approved to be sent to the area.

Sri Lankan officials said 2,500 Tamil refugees had made the narrow crossing between Sri Lanka and India's southern state of Tamil Nadu since July, when the army first launched its offensive on Kilinochchi.
Sri Lanka has accused the LTTE of forcing the exodus of Tamils and intensified naval patrols to stop illegal entry into India.

With 50 million Tamil-speakers, Tamil Nadu has provided a sanctuary for both Tamil residents and rebels since the ethnic war started in 1983. Some 200,000 refugees arrived in Tamil Nadu in the 1980s and many are still in camps there.
But Indian sympathy soured after the 1991 murder of former Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi by a suspected LTTE female suicide bomber during an election campaign in the state.
